# useToggle

> Cycle through a boolean or a fixed tuple of values (`light → dark → system`).

🟢 beginner · React 16.8+ · Custom Hooks › State utilities · support: universal

**Playground:** `npm run dev` → [`#/entry/use-toggle`](http://localhost:5173/#/entry/use-toggle)

## Concept

Stores the _index_ of the current value; `toggle` advances it modulo the list length and `setValue` jumps to a value found with `Object.is`.

## Problem

Cycling logic (`values[(values.indexOf(v) + 1) % values.length]`) gets rewritten in every component and breaks when the list is an inline array or contains `NaN`.

## When to use

- Theme switchers, sort direction (`asc → desc → none`), view modes, simple switches.

## When not to use

- You need `setTrue`/`setFalse` style actions for a boolean — use `useBoolean`.
- The set of values is dynamic or user-defined — use `useState` with a union type.

## API

```ts
function useToggle(
  initialValue?: boolean,
): readonly [boolean, () => void, (value: boolean) => void];
function useToggle<const T extends readonly [unknown, unknown, ...unknown[]]>(
  values: T,
  initialValue?: T[number],
): readonly [T[number], () => void, (value: T[number]) => void];
```

| Parameter                   | Type                   | Description                                                             |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `values` _(optional)_       | `readonly [A, B, ...]` | Two or more values. Inline arrays are fine; literal types are inferred. |
| `initialValue` _(optional)_ | `boolean \| T[number]` | Starting value (default: the first value / `false`).                    |

**Returns:** `[value, toggle, setValue]`. `toggle` ignores arguments.

## Edge cases

- `setValue` with a value not in the list is ignored (with a development warning).
- If the list gets shorter, the stored index wraps with modulo.
- Fewer than two values throws a `RangeError`.
